With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. The Fed’s choice to keep the policy rate at the effective lower bound and continue large-scale purchases is broadly consistent with Taylor-style prescriptions in the presence of a large output gap and the determinacy/expectations-stabilization results in New Keynesian models (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler; Woodford). Emphasis on Treasuries and MBS aligns with the credit channel and financial-frictions literature showing that easing spreads and supporting market functioning can bolster real activity (Bernanke and Gertler; Monacelli). However, the literature also cautions that mismeasured slack and supply shocks can render “transitory” inflation more persistent, requiring a sufficiently strong policy response to keep expectations anchored (Orphanides; Taylor principle; Lubik and Schorfheide). Net tone: cautiously constructive.
